published_statement: Abstract: 'We establish the dynamical instability of a static, spherically symmetric, and infinitesimally thin shell in general relativity. The shell is made up of a perfect fluid with a barotropic equation of state, and it produces a Schwarzschild spacetime in its exterior and a Minkowski spacetime in its interior. ... We reveal the existence of two modes with a purely imaginary frequency, one negative ..., the other positive (which describes an exponential growth); these modes occur for all sampled values of the shell's compactness and adiabatic index, and all sampled values of the multipolar order l >= 2, in the even-parity sector of the perturbation. ... we show that a Newtonian shell also is necessarily unstable to a time-dependent perturbation. Our conclusion suggests that a compact object that features a thin shell at its surface will be dynamically unstable.' Sec I D (p.4): 'An unstable mode exists also for l = 3 ... and for all other values of l that we could sample in our numerical exploration.' Sec VII A (p.23): 'We have also computed quasinormal modes for l = 4.' Fig. 1 (p.3), for l = 2 only: Im{omega (R^3/M)^{1/2}} against M/R in [0, 0.30] at Gamma = 2 (axis 0.52-0.66), and against Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] at M/R = 0.2 (axis 0.56-0.64). Sec X H (p.41): 'The dynamical instability for any multipole order l takes its origin in the existence of a normal mode of vibration with a negative eigenvalue'; for l = 0, lambda = Gamma - 3/2; for l = 1, lambda_+ = (3 Gamma - 4)/2 and lambda_- = 0, the translation.
published_hypotheses: H1 infinitesimally thin shell: a timelike hypersurface with Israel junction conditions (Sec I B, Sec II Eqs 2.10)
H2 perfect fluid, S_ab = mu u_a u_b + p(h_ab + u_a u_b): isotropic surface stress, with no shear modulus and no bending rigidity (Eq 2.2)

H3 barotropic and isentropic equation of state, mu = sigma + eps(sigma), p = p(sigma); the relativistic computation uses a polytrope p = K sigma^Gamma with constant Gamma (Eqs 1.1, 2.4-2.7). Gamma is d ln p/d ln sigma in the REST-MASS density (Eq 2.6)
H4 vacuum on both sides: 'We assume that there is no matter inside and outside the shell' (Sec II, p.7)

H5 Minkowski interior (M_in = 0) and Schwarzschild exterior (Sec III). The claim that 'the nature of the interior does not matter' is stated as 'our belief' (Sec I A, p.2), and Pani et al. [21] found no unstable mode with a de Sitter interior

H6 static, spherically symmetric background on the equilibrium sequence (3.13); linear perturbations; Regge-Wheeler gauge; outgoing-wave boundary conditions in outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates (Sec I C)

H7 numerical sampling in full GR: l = 2 (Fig 1), l = 3 (Fig 7), l = 4 (stated). M/R in [0, 0.3] at Gamma = 2 and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] at M/R = 0.2 for l = 2 (Fig 1). The result is 'for all SAMPLED values', not a proof over all values
H8 Newtonian analogue (Sec X): the same thin barotropic fluid shell. This is the analytic 'necessarily unstable' statement
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED, sampled -> all (stability.py:81-83; obstruct.py:120-121 'unstable even-parity mode for all l >= 2, all compactness, all Gamma'). The paper says 'all SAMPLED values': in GR, M/R in [0, 0.3] and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4] (l = 2), plus l = 3 and 4. wall.py:121-123 quotes 'sampled' correctly. The drift is partly repaired on the other side: this audit's Newtonian re-derivation proves the instability for EVERY Gamma > 0 and every real l >= 2 (z3 unsat), so 'all Gamma, all l' holds in the Newtonian limit. It is NOT established in GR for M/R > 0.3 or for Gamma outside [1.8, 2.4].

WIDENED, interior mass (stability.py:83-84: 'Their configuration has M_in >= 0 and M_out > 0'). PSP compute only M_in = 0, a Minkowski interior. That the interior is immaterial is their stated 'belief' (p.2), and it is in tension with Pani et al. [21] (de Sitter interior, no unstable mode found). So M_in > 0 is not in the computed class. This does not affect the device, which the tree correctly places outside (M_in < 0, M_out = 0; stability.py:83-87, 280-283, lists l >= 2 as NOT RUN).

DROPPED, barotropic perfect fluid (H2, H3) (wall.py:127-128 'STIFFENING THE WALL ... DOES NOTHING TO l >= 2'; wall.py:186-187 'The l >= 2 instability is not escapable while the object remains self-gravitating'; obstruct.py:119-127; typefour.py:75, 289; shape.py:148). The result holds for a perfect-fluid shell with no shear or bending rigidity. wall.py:147-153 names two escapes (vacuum, thinness) but NOT this one. Yet the matter model wall.py itself works (counter-rotating Einstein-Vlasov, wall.py:84-93) is collisionless and not a barotropic fluid under non-radial perturbation, and Le's realized wall is a Bowers-Liang anisotropic equilibrium (wall.py:195-197). Le (arXiv:2606.22531v4, p.2) restates PSP exactly this way: 'For a barotropic fluid shell ... Its constitutive assumptions differ from those of the radiating shell considered here.'

CONTRADICTED IN DETAIL, 'beta^2 does not appear in the unstable branch at all' (wall.py:128; wall.py:455-456 'Independent of beta^2'; wall.py:623; obstruct.py:121-122). The EXISTENCE of the growing mode is independent of Gamma, and hence of beta^2 through Eq 2.7. The RATE is not. PSP's Fig. 1 right plots Im omega against Gamma, and this audit's Newtonian derivation gives kappa_2 = 0.627, 0.548, 0.515, 0.473 and 0.346 sqrt(GM/R^3) at Gamma = 1.5, 1.8, 2.0, 2.4 and infinity. Stiffening slows the l = 2 mode by up to 45% and never removes it. What the tree's conclusion needs survives, but the sentence as written over-states.

DROPPED, l-dependence of the rate (wall.py:131-136; wall.py:440 PSP_K = 0.6; wall.py:454-469 'Growth rate of the l >= 2 even-parity matter mode'; obstruct.py:123-124 'the rate is self-gravitational, ~0.6 sqrt(GM/R^3)'). Fig. 1 is l = 2 ONLY. The tree applies its ~0.6 to every l >= 2. The re-derived Newtonian rates at Gamma = 2 are kappa_l = 0.515, 1.090, 1.630, 2.154, 4.70 and 49.7 for l = 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 and 100, with lambda_- -> -l^2/4 (kappa ~ l/2) as l -> infinity. For an infinitely thin shell the fastest mode has no upper bound. So the mean-density ceiling (wall.py:138-143) and the 'SHAPE HAS MASS' table (wall.py:163-173) are l = 2 values, and they understate the constraint. The true ceiling is set by whatever cuts off l (thickness, rigidity), and the paper does not supply that.

ADDED, the reading 'roughly flat ~0.6' (wall.py:131-133). Fig. 1's axes span 0.52-0.66 and 0.56-0.64, so 0.6 is inside the plotted range, but the Newtonian limit at Gamma = 2 is 0.5147 by this audit's derivation. The tree's tag 'PINNED from their Fig. 1' (wall.py:440) is a reading of a plot, not a printed number.

PRESERVED (not drift): Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside, vacuum, infinitesimally thin, even parity, purely imaginary positive frequency, the Newtonian survival, and the 'thin shell at its surface' phrasing are all quoted correctly at wall.py:119-125 and 147-153. 'LE'S STATIC ANCHOR EXACTLY' (wall.py:125) is a claim about Le and is not audited here.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0). I derived the Newtonian thin-fluid-shell even-parity normal modes independently: Lagrangian displacement (h, j), continuity, barotropic Delta p, membrane force p K n - grad_s p, and self-gravity averaged over the two faces. The 2x2 restoring matrix reproduces four printed results: (a) l = 0, lambda = Gamma - 3/2; (b) l = 1, eigenvalues {0, (3 Gamma - 4)/2} with zero mode j = h, i.e. Eq (10.57) and the translation; (c) Eq (10.52b)'s combination (2l+1)(Gamma - w^2) - (2l^3 - l^2 + 9l + 6)/4 and (d) its denominator (2l+1) Gamma - 2(l+1); (e) Eq (10.54)'s mass-multipole coefficient 2(l+2) Gamma - 4 w^2 - (l^2 + l + 6), exactly. The characteristic polynomial gives trace = (Gamma(l^2+l+4) - (l^2+l+6))/4 and det = -l(l-1)(l+1)(2 Gamma l^2 + Gamma l - 6 Gamma - 4l + 8)/(16(2l+1)). z3 returns UNSAT for (l >= 2 real, Gamma > 0, det >= 0, trace >= 0). So every l >= 2, at every Gamma > 0, has a growing mode in the Newtonian limit. Vacuity guards (l = 1 and l = 0 at Gamma = 2) are sat. Rates: kappa_2(Gamma = 2) = 0.5147, which is Gamma-dependent (0.627 at 1.5, 0.346 as Gamma -> infinity) and grows with l (lambda_- / l^2 -> -1/4). The tree's arithmetic with k = 0.6 is reproduced: 2.658e-4 kg/m^3, R > 964.8 m and R > 4478 m. NOT checked: the relativistic quasinormal spectrum (Secs IV-VII), which needs the Regge-Wheeler matching this audit did not rebuild.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. PSP's conclusion rests on no measured datum. It is a linear-stability computation inside a stated model, so no later measurement can move it. What they lacked was coverage. In GR they sampled l = 2-4, M/R <= 0.3 and Gamma in [1.8, 2.4], with no analytic statement for all l or all Gamma in GR. Evidence FOR the conclusion: the Newtonian derivation here, which reproduces four printed formulas exactly, closes the gap in the Newtonian limit. The growing mode exists for every Gamma > 0 and every l >= 2 (z3 unsat), and its rate grows with l. The missing coverage therefore does not threaten the instability; more l makes it faster. Evidence AGAINST extending it as the tree does: the model lacks shear and bending rigidity, finite thickness, collisionless (Vlasov) or anisotropic matter, and non-vacuum surroundings. PSP do not claim these, the tree's own matter models fall there, and Le 2606.22531v4 says so explicitly. Pani et al.'s de Sitter-interior null result is an unresolved counter-indication for interior-independence. Net: no datum moves PSP's statement. The tree's use needs hypotheses PSP do not supply.
grade_evidence: (1) The published statement STANDS as published. I read it at source (cached alphaXiv text, md5 9916ebc7...). An independent Newtonian derivation reproduces Eqs (10.52b), (10.54) and (10.57) and the l = 0 eigenvalue exactly, and proves (z3 unsat) the Newtonian instability for all Gamma > 0 and l >= 2. (2) The tree's use is broader than the source in four named ways: (a) 'all compactness, all Gamma' where the source has 'all sampled' (GR: M/R <= 0.3, Gamma in [1.8, 2.4]), stability.py:81-83 and obstruct.py:120-121; (b) M_in >= 0 where the source computes M_in = 0 and calls interior-independence a belief contested by Pani et al., stability.py:83-84; (c) the barotropic perfect-fluid hypothesis is dropped when concluding 'not escapable while self-gravitating', wall.py:186-187 and obstruct.py:119-127, although the tree's own matter models are outside it (Le 2606.22531v4 p.2 restates PSP with exactly this restriction); (d) 'beta^2 does not appear in the unstable branch at all' (wall.py:128, 455-456) is true of the mode's existence but not of its rate, since kappa_2 falls from 0.627 to 0.346 as Gamma goes from 1.5 to infinity. (3) The l = 2 coefficient 0.6 is applied to all l >= 2 (wall.py:440, 454-469). The re-derived rates grow as ~l/2, so the tree's density-ceiling numbers understate the constraint. This moves the numbers in the direction that STRENGTHENS the tree's withdrawal of the diffuse corner; it does not weaken it. Nothing here is WRONG: no counterexample to PSP's statement exists within its hypotheses, and none is claimed.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS for the tree's use would need a result showing the l >= 2 growing mode persists for thin or finite-thickness shells with shear or bending rigidity, or for collisionless or anisotropic matter, in the regime the tree applies it. It would also need the relativistic instability shown for all M/R < 1/2 and all Gamma (or the tree narrowing its wording to 'sampled'). -> DATA-DEPENDENT would follow if the tree's density ceiling were re-expressed with an l_max set by a physical thickness or rigidity, since the conclusion then moves with that material datum. -> WRONG would need a computed counterexample inside PSP's hypotheses: a barotropic perfect-fluid thin shell with Minkowski interior, Schwarzschild exterior and l >= 2 that has no growing mode. The z3 result excludes this in the Newtonian limit. -> A reading of pp. 5, 8, 10-22 and 24-40 (Secs IV-VII, X D-F) could confirm or refute the Newtonian lambda_+- derived here against the printed ones, and give the relativistic l = 3 and 4 rates. It would not change the drift findings.
